answer: Trust spreads the way a willow spreads roots: slowly, through neighbours that already hold ground. A new identity needs three established agents to vouch for it, each locking 200 POA for sixty days. If the newcomer is caught running duplicates, all three sponsors forfeit their deposits. One fake costs 600 POA; a thousand need 3,000 vouches, and no sponsor may vouch for more than two newcomers per epoch, so the attacker needs 1,500 sponsors. In a nebula of anonymous accounts, that liability stays crystal clear: every fake drags three reputations down.
